--- title: "Estimated Marginal Means with `emmeans`" subtitle: "PSYC 6019-A01 / PSYC 6022-A01
2026-10-23 | Lab 9" author: "Jess Helmer" footer: "[jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026](https://jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026/)" format: revealjs: code-link: true slide-number: true code-line-numbers: false theme: ../../gt-theme.scss width: 1200 execute: echo: true dpi: 600 freeze: auto knitr: opts_chunk: dev: svg --- ## Outline - `emmeans` with One-Way ANOVA - `emmeans` with Two-Way ANOVA ::: {.cell} ::: # One-Way ANOVA `emmeans` ## Estimated Marginal Means EMMs, also known as "least-squares means" For a One-Way ANOVA, this is the same as just looking at the means of our groups. ::: subpoint ○ Will get a bit more complicated with more than just one factor... ::: Useful to report with your ANOVA results to actually see the differences between means. ## Estimated Marginal Means Remember those interpretations of slope parameters? :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Dummy coding compares $g-1$ groups to $\beta_0 =$ **reference group mean**: | Predictor | $g_1$ | $g_2$ | $\cdots$ | $g_{G-1}$ | $g_G$ | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | $x_1$ | 1 | 0 | $\cdots$ | 0 | 0 | | $x_2$ | 0 | 1 | $\cdots$ | 0 | 0 | | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\ddots$ | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | | $x_{G-1}$ | 0 | 0 | $\cdots$ | 1 | 0 | ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Dummy coding:** - $\beta_0: = \mu_3$ - $\beta_1: = \mu_{1} - \mu_3$ - $\beta_2: = \mu_{2} - \mu_3$ ::: :::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Effects or contrast coding compares $g-1$ groups to $\beta_0 =$ **grand mean**: | Predictor | $g_1$ | $g_2$ | $\cdots$ | $g_{G-1}$ | $g_G$ | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | $x_1$ | 1 | 0 | $\cdots$ | 0 | -1 | | $x_2$ | 0 | 1 | $\cdots$ | 0 | -1 | | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\ddots$ | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | | $x_{G-1}$ | 0 | 0 | $\cdots$ | 1 | -1 | ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Contrast/Effects coding:** - $\beta_0: = \mu$ - $\beta_1: = \mu_{1} - \mu$ - $\beta_2: = \mu_{2} - \mu$ Compares groups to **grand mean** ::: :::: The means calculated from the slope parameters are the Estimated Marginal Means (EMMs). ::: footer [Stolen from Mark's slides](https://jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026/lecture/slides/16%20One%20Way%20ANOVA/Lecture%2016%20One%20Way%20ANOVA_v0.html#/coding-options) ::: ## One-Way ANOVA Recall from last time... ::: {.cell layout-ncol="2"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palmerpenguins) penguins_cleaned <- penguins |> filter_out(when_any(is.na(flipper_length_mm), is.na(species))) flipper_model <- aov(flipper_length_mm ~ species, data = penguins_cleaned) flipper_model_lm <- lm(flipper_length_mm ~ species, data = penguins_cleaned) summary(flipper_model); summary(flipper_model_lm) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F) species 2 52473 26237 594.8 <2e-16 *** Residuals 339 14953 44 --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = flipper_length_mm ~ species, data = penguins_cleaned) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -17.9536 -4.8235 0.0464 4.8130 20.0464 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 189.9536 0.5405 351.454 < 2e-16 *** speciesChinstrap 5.8699 0.9699 6.052 3.79e-09 *** speciesGentoo 27.2333 0.8067 33.760 < 2e-16 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 6.642 on 339 degrees of freedom Multiple R-squared: 0.7782, Adjusted R-squared: 0.7769 F-statistic: 594.8 on 2 and 339 DF, p-value: < 2.2e-16 ``` ::: ::: Let's get the estimated marginal means of penguin flipper length by species! ## EMMs in R To obtain the EMMs for some linear model: `emmeans::emmeans(model, specs)` ::: subpoint ○ `model` = linear model object (e.g., from `lm()`, `aov()`, or `stan_glm()`) ::: ::: subpoint ○ `specs` = predictors for which you want estimated marginal means :::
::: {.callout-note style="font-size: 80%"} ### `emmeans` and pipes `|>` While we often want to use pipes in our `R` code, and e.g., might want to plot the EMMs from `emmeans`, the developers explicity recommend to always manually check the output of the `emmeans` function! They provide annotations and context that we will lose if we immediately pipe it into something else (e.g., `emmeans(model, specs) |> as_tibble()`) ::: ## One-Way ANOVA `emmeans` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages("emmeans") library(emmeans) emms_flipper <- emmeans(flipper_model, specs = "species") emms_flipper ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` species emmean SE df lower.CL upper.CL Adelie 190 0.540 339 189 191 Chinstrap 196 0.805 339 194 197 Gentoo 217 0.599 339 216 218 Confidence level used: 0.95 ``` ::: ::: ## Plotting One-Way `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Super quick plotting method with `plot()`. Points are Estimated Marginal Means, and bars are confidence intervals for those EMMs. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(emms_flipper) ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Returns a `ggplot`, so you can work with it from there. But don't have muchhh control over the geometries (`geom`s) or mapping (`mapping = aes()`). Feel free to check out the documentation at [rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/reference/plot.html](https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/reference/plot.html) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(emms_flipper) + scale_x_continuous("Estimated Marginal Mean", limits = c(180, 230)) + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(NULL, cap = T)) + theme_classic(base_size = 14) ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Can also easily make ourselves by converting the `emmeans` object into a `tibble` (again, after we've looked at it ourselves!) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_df <- as_tibble(emms_flipper) emms_flipper_df |> glimpse() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 3 Columns: 6 $ species Adelie, Chinstrap, Gentoo $ emmean 189.9536, 195.8235, 217.1870 $ SE 0.5404799, 0.8054037, 0.5988465 $ df 339, 339, 339 $ lower.CL 188.8905, 194.2393, 216.0091 $ upper.CL 191.0168, 197.4077, 218.3649 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.fragment fragment-index=2} If plotting points, we always want to include our uncertainty. ::: ::: ::: {.column .fragment fragment-index=1 width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-8-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_df |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = emmean)) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} `geom_errorbar(mapping = aes(x, ymin, ymax), width = 0.9)` ::: subpoint-narrow ○ Alternatively, can specify `aes(y, xmin, xmin)` to flip the other way ::: ::: subpoint-narrow ○ `width` = width of error bar, may want to shrink `width` below its default ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_df |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = emmean, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL)) + geom_errorbar() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Can layer `geom_point` on top, tidy up ::: subpoint-narrow ○ `geom_point` will need a `y` `aes` (or `x` if it's flipped) ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-12-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_df |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = emmean, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL, color = species)) + geom_errorbar(width = 0.1) + geom_point() + scale_y_continuous("EMM of Flipper Length", limits = c(180, 230)) + guides(x = guide_axis(NULL, cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Or add in the original data too... ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-14-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_df |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = emmean, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL, color = species)) + geom_violin(data = penguins_cleaned, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = species), alpha = 0.2, color = NA, inherit.aes = F) + geom_jitter(data = penguins_cleaned, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, color = species), alpha = 0.15, shape = 21, size = 1.5, inherit.aes = F) + geom_errorbar(width = 0.1) + geom_point() + scale_y_continuous("EMM of Flipper Length", limits = c(180, 230)) + guides(x = guide_axis(NULL, cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Or add in the original data too... ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_df |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = emmean, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL, color = species)) + geom_violin(data = penguins_cleaned, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = species), alpha = 0.2, color = NA, inherit.aes = F) + geom_jitter(data = penguins_cleaned, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, color = species), alpha = 0.15, shape = 21, size = 1.5, inherit.aes = F) + geom_errorbar(width = 0.1) + geom_point() + scale_y_continuous("EMM of Flipper Length", limits = c(180, 230)) + guides(x = guide_axis(NULL, cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Pairwise Comparisons With `emmeans` `pairs(emmeans_object, adjust = "tukey")` ::: subpoint-narrow ○ Equivalent to `emmeans::contrast(emmeans_object, method = "pairwise)` ::: ::: subpoint-narrow ○ `adjust` = can supply name of adjustment ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairs(emms_flipper) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` contrast estimate SE df t.ratio p.value Adelie - Chinstrap -5.87 0.970 339 -6.052 <0.0001 Adelie - Gentoo -27.23 0.807 339 -33.760 <0.0001 Chinstrap - Gentoo -21.36 1.000 339 -21.286 <0.0001 P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates ``` ::: ::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairs(emms_flipper, adjust = "bonf") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` contrast estimate SE df t.ratio p.value Adelie - Chinstrap -5.87 0.970 339 -6.052 <0.0001 Adelie - Gentoo -27.23 0.807 339 -33.760 <0.0001 Chinstrap - Gentoo -21.36 1.000 339 -21.286 <0.0001 P value adjustment: bonferroni method for 3 tests ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairs(emms_flipper, adjust = "holm") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` contrast estimate SE df t.ratio p.value Adelie - Chinstrap -5.87 0.970 339 -6.052 <0.0001 Adelie - Gentoo -27.23 0.807 339 -33.760 <0.0001 Chinstrap - Gentoo -21.36 1.000 339 -21.286 <0.0001 P value adjustment: holm method for 3 tests ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: # Two-Way ANOVA `emmeans` ## Two-Way ANOVA `emmeans` [EMMs theoretically in context of two-way ANOVA] ## Two-Way ANOVA :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} So far we've looked at penguin species, but these penguin measurements were taken over multiple years. What if the year a penguin's measurement was taken is in some way linked to the penguin's flipper length? ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ![](../media/lab_09/penguin-islands.png) ::: :::: ::: footer Photo accessed at [rpubs.com/mgsaavedraro/669873](https://rpubs.com/mgsaavedraro/669873) on 2026-10-15. ::: ## Two-Way ANOVA Let's examine the effect of both penguin species and measurement year on penguin flipper length. Design: Two-Way 3x3 ANOVA ## Two-Way ANOVA :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palmerpenguins) penguins_cleaned <- penguins |> filter_out(when_any(is.na(year), is.na(flipper_length_mm), is.na(species))) |> mutate(year = factor(year)) flipper_model_twoway <- aov(flipper_length_mm ~ species * year, data = penguins_cleaned) summary(flipper_model_twoway) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F) species 2 52473 26237 651.974 < 2e-16 *** year 2 1464 732 18.190 3.18e-08 *** species:year 4 89 22 0.551 0.698 Residuals 333 13401 40 --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Let's get the estimated marginal means of penguin flipper length by species and year! ::: :::: ## One-Way ANOVA `emmeans` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_twoway <- emmeans(flipper_model_twoway, specs = c("species", "year")) emms_flipper_twoway ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` species year emmean SE df lower.CL upper.CL Adelie 2007 187 0.906 333 185 188 Chinstrap 2007 192 1.240 333 190 195 Gentoo 2007 215 1.090 333 213 217 Adelie 2008 191 0.897 333 189 193 Chinstrap 2008 198 1.500 333 195 201 Gentoo 2008 218 0.935 333 216 219 Adelie 2009 192 0.880 333 190 194 Chinstrap 2009 198 1.290 333 196 201 Gentoo 2009 218 0.967 333 217 220 Confidence level used: 0.95 ``` ::: ::: ## Plotting One-Way ANOVA `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Super quick plotting method with `plot()` Not so great with more than one factor... ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-23-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(emms_flipper_twoway) ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way ANOVA `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Let's build our own. The color on our last plot was just to make it look nice, but this time, let's use color to represent the year. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_twoway_df <- as_tibble(emms_flipper_twoway) emms_flipper_twoway_df |> glimpse() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 9 Columns: 7 $ species Adelie, Chinstrap, Gentoo, Adelie, Chinstrap, Gentoo, Adelie,… $ year 2007, 2007, 2007, 2008, 2008, 2008, 2009, 2009, 2009 $ emmean 186.5918, 192.4231, 215.1176, 191.0400, 197.7222, 217.5652, 1… $ SE 0.9062353, 1.2440915, 1.0879265, 0.8971272, 1.4952119, 0.9353… $ df 333, 333, 333, 333, 333, 333, 333, 333, 333 $ lower.CL 184.8092, 189.9758, 212.9776, 189.2752, 194.7810, 215.7253, 1… $ upper.CL 188.3745, 194.8703, 217.2577, 192.8048, 200.6635, 219.4051, 1… ``` ::: ::: ::: {.fragment fragment-index=2} Like last time, we always want to include our uncertainty. ::: ::: ::: {.column .fragment fragment-index=1 width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-26-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_twoway_df |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = emmean, color = year)) + geom_point() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way ANOVA `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Let's build our own. ::: ::: {.column .fragment fragment-index=1 width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-28-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_twoway_df |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = emmean, color = year, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL)) + geom_point() + geom_errorbar() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way ANOVA `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Let's build our own. And tidy it up. ::: ::: {.column .fragment fragment-index=1 width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-30-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_twoway_df |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = emmean, color = year, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL)) + geom_point(position = position_dodge(0.3)) + geom_errorbar(width = 0.1, position = position_dodge(0.3)) + scale_y_continuous("EMM of Flipper Length", limits = c(180, 230)) + guides(x = guide_axis(NULL, cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Plotting One-Way ANOVA `emmeans` :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Can add lines between points to look for interactions. ::: ::: {.column .fragment fragment-index=1 width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_09_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-32-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} emms_flipper_twoway_df |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = emmean, color = year, group = year, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL)) + geom_point(position = position_dodge(0.3)) + geom_line(position = position_dodge(0.3)) + geom_errorbar(width = 0.1, position = position_dodge(0.3)) + scale_y_continuous("EMM of Flipper Length", limits = c(180, 230)) + guides(x = guide_axis(NULL, cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Pairwise Comparisons With `emmeans` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairs(emms_flipper_twoway) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` contrast estimate SE df t.ratio p.value Adelie year2007 -
